problem.headline: You've worked with designers before. Some were fast. Some were pretty. None of them asked you why.

columns.label: The Pixel Pusher
columns.body: Renders your brief. Won't push back. Ships something that looks like the reference.

columns.label: The Stylist
columns.body: Makes it pretty. Has a Dribbble. Can't tell you why the button works — only that it's on-trend.

columns.label: The Hand-off Artist
columns.body: Beautiful Figma. Devs cry. Half the screens don't ship. Calls it 'a developer problem.'

method.headline: Four moves. In order. Every project.

steps.title: See
steps.body: Audit the brand, the product, the customer, the board. Find what's actually being avoided.

steps.title: Solve
steps.body: Reframe the problem until the answer is obvious. Then design the smallest thing that proves it.

steps.title: Systemize
steps.body: Turn the solution into infrastructure — tokens, components, patterns the team can extend without me.

steps.title: Scale
steps.body: Ship it live. Measure. Cut what underperforms. Compound what works. Repeat next quarter.

manifesto.headline: Ten principles for designers who refuse to be replaced.
principles: Refuse the brief. Demand the question.
Systems over screens. Screens over stickers.
If it doesn't ship, it didn't happen.
Make the trade-off visible before you make the trade-off.
Polarize on purpose. Pleasing everyone serves no one.
Read the room before you redesign it.
Edit aggressively. Especially your own taste.
Be the designer founders call when the deck is on the table.
